message.content:
<think>The user wants me to find the bug in this JavaScript function that should return the maximum of an array but always returns the first element.

Let me analyze the code:

```js
function maxOf(arr) {
  let max = arr[0];
  for (let i = 1; i < arr.length; i++) {
    if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[0];  // BUG HERE!
  }
  return max;
}
```

The bug is on this line:
```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[0];
```

When a new maximum is found (when `max < arr[i]`), it should assign `arr[i]` to `max`, not `arr[0]`.

The correct line should be:
```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[i];
```

This is a simple typo/logical error where the developer accidentally wrote `arr[0]` instead of `arr[i]`.
</think>

# Bug Found

The bug is on **line 4**. When a new maximum is found, the code assigns `arr[0]` instead of `arr[i]` to `max`.

## The Problem

```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[0];  // ❌ Always assigns first element
```

## The Fix

```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[i];  // ✅ Assigns the current (larger) element
```

## Corrected Function

```js
function maxOf(arr) {
  let max = arr[0];
  for (let i = 1; i < arr.length; i++) {
    if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[i];  // Fixed: arr[i] instead of arr[0]
  }
  return max;
}
```

This is a simple typo where `arr[0]` was written instead of `arr[i]`.
